Commentary.Commentary: We are done with the ODI series. It is Bangladesh who have won it 3-0 and Zimbabwe have now lost 13 matches on the trot. Both the teams now will turn their attention to the longest format which will begin on the 3rd of November. The first Test will be played in Sylhet at 0930 local (0330 GMT). Till then take care and goodbye!

Imrul Kayes is the unanimous choice for the Man of the Series award. He is glad to get a chance to prove himself. Adds further he wanted to do something for the team and is happy with how he has played. Credits the way Sarkar batted and says he released all the pressure. Hopes to do well in the Test series as well.

Man of the Match, Soumya Sarkar says he is very pleased with his performance as he was out of the team before this game. Ends by saying the wicket was really good to bat on and he enjoyed batting out there.

Zimbabwe's skipper, Hamilton Masakadza says the defeat today was tough as they batted well. Mentions Kayes and Sarkar batted really well and they took the game away from them. He feels the batters will head into the Test format with some confidence and hopes that the players added to the squad will bring some luck.

Earlier in the day, it was a strong batting performance from Zimbabwe. Powered by Sean Williams' century and his partnerships with Taylor, Raza and Moor, they managed to post a challenging total on the board. However, their bowlers failed to turn up and they suffered yet another massive loss.

The pair of Kayes and Sarkar went after the bowlers right from the outset and both notched up their centuries. Sarkar, in particular, was in blazing form, amassing 6 maximums in his knock of 117 as he took the Zimbabwean bowlers to the cleaners. Kayes was initially the aggressor but once Sarkar got going, the former was happy to play second fiddle. The duo, however, could not stay there till the end as one perished shortly after getting to his ton and the other got dismissed with just 13 needed for a win. However, Rahim and Mithun ensured they did not lose any more wickets and finished the game off with ease.

BANGLADESH INFLICT A CLEAN SWEEP! A mockery, that is exactly what Bangladesh have made of this run chase. This is the highest run chase on this ground and they have done it without breaking a sweat. At the start though, they lost their first wicket on the very first ball of the chase, but then Soumya Sarkar and Imrul Kayes joined forces and smashed a record partnership of 220 runs.

SIX! Rahim finishes it off in style! Short ball on middle, Rahim goes back and pulls it over the mid-wicket fence for a biggie. Customary handshakes all around as BANGLADESH WIN BY 7 WICKETS WITH 47 BALLS LEFT!
FOUR! 5 more needed! A low full toss on the pads, Mithun lofts it over mid on and a boundary results.
A low full toss on middle, Mithun finds covers with his drive.
Fires it on off, kept out.
Comes down the track and tries to go inside out. It goes off the inner half towards mid-wicket for a brace. Runs needed below 10.
Slower through the air on off, Rahim guides it to point.
On the pads, worked to mid-wicket.
Three dots! Rahim pushes it towards covers. He wants a run but is sent back.
On off, defended. Bangladesh are in no hurry here.
Flatter on off, kept out.
Eases this down to long off for a run.
Dances down the track but does not get to the pitch of it. He drives it to covers.
Flatter and outside off, Rahim punches it through covers for a run.
Powerplay 3 has been signaled! Now 5 fielders can be placed outside the ring. Not sure if that would make a difference to the outcome of the game.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Flighted and full on off, defended off the front foot.
Dropped? Short and outside off, Mithun tries to play the square cut but fails to connect. Taylor also fails to collect the ball cleanly. Not too sure there was an outside edge.
Mohammad Mithun is the new batsman.

OUT! So Kayes does not finish it off. Something to rejoice for Zimbabwe. End of a magnificent innings. He tries to end it early by dancing down the track, tries to clear long off but does not get the desired elevation. Elton Chigumbura settles underneath it near the rope and takes the catch easily. End of a wonderful knock and Raza congratulates Kayes on his way back. 13 more needed.
Flatter on middle, works it to mid-wicket.
Around off, the batsman taps it towards point and gets to the other end.
Slower through the air again, Rahim guides it through backward point and takes a run.
Fires it on off, Rahim defends it onto the ground.
On the pads again, flicked through mid-wicket and the batsmen cross over.
FOUR! TOP SHOT! Floated up outside off, Kayes beats the diving mid off fielder and a boundary results. Runs needed now below 20.
Fires it on the pads, Kayes works it to short fine leg.
Down the leg side and it has been wided.
Shortish and outside off again, Williams cuts it through point for a run.
Driven down to long off for a run. 22 more needed.
Works it through square leg for a run.
Driven through mid on by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Eased through mid on for a single.
Shorter outside off, Rahim tries to cut but it goes off the toe end through covers for a run.

NOT OUT! Umpire's call as it is clipping the bails. Zimbabwe do not lose a review. It was more out of desperation though. This was bowled slower through the air around middle, it pitches and then turns. Rahim is beaten on the outside edge as he tries to defend and the ball hits him high on the back leg. The players appeal but the umpire is not interested. After a long thought, Masakadza signals the 'T'. Replays roll in and it does not show three reds. So the on-field call remains.
A late review as an appeal for an LBW has been turned down. Rahim is the man in question.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Stroked towards cover for a run.
Eases it down to long off for a run.
Another short ball, Kayes mistimes his shot towards covers.
Slower through the air and it is again outside off, Rahim guides it towards backward point for a run.
Short and outside off, Rahim cuts but finds the fielder at cover-point.
Sikandar Raza is back on.
Fires it on the pads, Kayes flicks it to short fine leg. 11 from the over.
SIX! BANG! Got to his 100, now it is time to accelerate. Goes down on one knee and slog sweeps it over the mid-wicket fence. 30 more needed.
Slower through the air on off, Rahim guides it through point and gets to the other end.
Now he tucks it through mid-wicket for a single.
Shorter and outside off, the batsman cuts it through point and takes a single.
On the stumps, kept out.
Wide down the leg side, the keeper fails to collect and the batsmen take a run.
Wellington Masakadza is back on.
FOUR! Caressed! Full and outside off, not a good ball with all the fielders in the ring on the off side. Rahim slaps it through covers and the ball races away.

4th ODI century for Kayes. His second of this series, could have easily been his third had he not been dismissed in the 90s in the second ODI. He jumps in the air in delight, pumping his fist. He stands tall and tucks it around the corner for a run to get to that milestone. The crowd is going bonkers. What a series for Kayes!
Good length around off, Rahim guides it through backward point for a run.
Good length on off, Rahim defends it towards cover. He wants a run but is sent back by his partner.
Slower ball on the shorter side. Kayes pulls it towards fine leg for a run. He moves onto 99.
Goes full on the pads, Kayes tries to flick but closes the bat face a touch early. He gets a leading edge back towards the bowler.
Donaldo Tiripano is back on.
Full and around off, an arm ball, skidding back in, Rahim tries to keep it out but gets an inside edge onto the pads. A stifled appeal for an lbw, not given.
Tossed up ball on off, defended off the front foot.
Goes down on one knee, fetches it from outside off and sweeps it to mid-wicket. Finds the fielder inside the ring.
Flatter delivery, it's darted on off, Rahim pushes it off his front foot to covers.
Tossed up ball around leg, Kayes on the back foot and turns it in front of square leg for a single.
Fullish and on off, it's driven down to long off for a run.
Quicker one, full and on off, Rahim forces it down to long on and takes a single.
Leans forward to a full ball and opens the face of the bat to push it towards short third man. Still not able to find the gap.
Wide! A bit short and going down the leg side, Mushfiqur allows it through.
Another dot ball. This one stays low after landing around off, Rahim strokes from the back foot but straight to covers.
Flatter and shorter outside off, Rahim cracks it off his back foot but once again finds the cover fielder.
Tossed up ball outside off, Rahim gets forward and taps it down towards short third man.
Floated full ball outside off, Rahim drills his drive through the line but finds the cover fielder at the edge of the circle.
Tossed up ball on middle and leg, Imrul helps it to deep mid-wicket and keeps strike. Moves to 97.
Doing it in singles. Loopy and on middle, Kayes knocks it down to long on for a run.
Darts it on the pads and Rahim flicks it to deep mid-wicket for one.
Flatter and outside off, punched from the crease but straight to covers.
Fires in a short ball on middle, quicker in pace, Kayes pulls it over mid-wicket for a run. Cannot get hold of his shot.
Oversteps and bowls a no ball. Rahim has tickled it through square leg for a run. Free Hit coming up...
Flighted on middle, worked on the leg side but straight to the fielder.

Bonus runs! Williams fires this one down the leg side, Kayes fails to get it away and the keeper also fails to collect. Masakadza chases it from short fine leg, puts in a slide near the fence and saves a run. Four added to the total.
Sean Williams is into the attack.
Full and flighted on middle, drifting in, Imrul drives it down to long off for one.
Slower through the air outside off, a bit on the shorter side, Kayes punches it from the crease but finds the cover fielder.
Flighted and full on off, Rahim strides forward and forces it down to long on for a single.
A touch short and on middle, Imrul helps it in front of square leg and crosses.
Flighted and full on middle, Kayes lunges and defends it on the leg side.
Quicker and flatter on the pads, Kayes nudges it through backward square leg and rushes back for the second run.
Drinks break. Meanwhile, Mushfiqur Rahim is in next at number 4. 67 needed off 120 balls.

OUT! Sarkar holes out! He was looking to dispatch everything into the stand but has miscued one. Anyway, what an outstanding knock by Soumya! He set the stadium on fire with his brilliant stroke play. Masakadza delivers a full ball in line of the stumps. It's bowled at a gentle pace and hence Sarkar has to generate all the power behind his shot. Ends up towering it in the air, it has more elevation than distance and Tiripano at long on catches the skier safely. Kayes pats his partner on the back. The crowd is on its feet. Crazy atmosphere.
Full and outside off, Sarkar goes hard at it with a drive and slices it towards short third man.
Makes room and strokes a length ball through covers for a run.
Kayes has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery. He's smelling yet another century in this series.
Exposes all his stumps to the bowler and Masakadza drops it on a length around off, Sarkar smashes it through covers for one.
A length ball angling away from the batsman, Kayes strokes it through covers and takes a single.
Hamilton Masakadza to bowl.
DOT BALL! Shortish and on middle, hit firmly across the line but straight to mid-wicket.

SIX! Another handsome shot! Raza serves a loopy ball around leg, Sarkar jumps out of the crease to take it on the full and absolutely hammers it deep into the stands at mid-wicket. This is mad hitting by Sarkar.
Goes on the back foot and slaps it to sweeper cover for one.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. They pick up a single.
SIX! Mighty hit! Once again Sarkar wears his skates to run down the track and smokes it over mid-wicket.
Flatter and fuller on middle, blocked back.
Slog swept but does not find the gap. The fielder in the deep mid-wicket region collects it and a run is taken.
Gets to the pitch of the ball and defends it.

EDGE AND RUNS! All going Bangladesh's way here. The arm ball on off, Sarkar tries to work it on the leg side but the ball takes the outside edge and goes towards short third man. The fielder misfields and two runs are taken.
The batsman works it down the leg side. One run added to the total.
Floats it up on middle, kept out.

100 for Sarkar. His second in this format and he is pumped up and why not? His first match of this series and he has announced his comeback into the team with some style. A brilliant knock, full of entertainment. A ton in just 81 balls. He flicks this through square leg to get to that milestone. He jumps in the air in delight as he completes the run. Can he stay there till the end though?
No, he does not but retains strike for the next over. Short and on middle, Sarkar pulls it through square leg for a run.
FOUR! Too easy for Sarkar. Again makes good use of the feet and hits it over mid-wicket for a boundary. 2 runs short of a ton now. He has one ball in this over. Will he bring it up?

Shorter but this one has a little more pace on it. Kayes is hurried into the pull as it hits him on the glove and goes down to fine leg for a run. This is now the best partnership for Bangladesh at home.
Back of a length again on middle, Sarkar guides it towards point for a single.
Back of a length on off, kept out.
FOUR! Another bowler who has been welcomed back into the attack with a boundary. Into the 90s is Sarkar. Short and on middle, Sarkar swivels and pulls it fine down the leg side.
Kyle Jarvis is back into the attack. Zimbabwe in dire straits, they need a wicket and that too in a heap, if they want to make a comeback.
Works this through mid-wicket and keeps strike. 14 from the over, 100 more needed in 144 balls. 9 wickets in hand. Zimbabwe need to get all 9 if they are to win this game. How? No idea.
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket.
Now pushes this back to the bowler. A DOT! Haven't been many in this partnership.
SIX! Two in a row! He wants to end this early. Again uses his feet, gets to the pitch of it and lofts it over the long on fence.
SIX! That is exactly why Kayes is giving the strike over to him because he is clearing the boundaries with ease. Uses his feet again and hits it over the long on fence. Moves into the 80s.
Fires this on the pads, Kayes is happy to nudge it around the corner and give the strike over to Sarkar.
On the pads, it is worked through square leg for a run.
FOUR! Too fine and the fielder has no chance. On the pads, easy pickings for a batsman in such good form. He flicks it towards fine leg and into the fence.
Shot but a good stop! Width on offer outside off, Sarkar slaps it towards covers. The fielder there makes a good half stop but can't stop the single.
Shortish and on middle, Kayes tucks it around the corner and takes a single.

Another length ball around middle, Kayes flicks it through mid-wicket for a couple. He now overtakes Tamim Iqbal to become the highest run scorer for Bangladesh in a bilateral ODI series. Going through a purple patch!
Back of a length around off, kept out.
Another misfield. The Zimbabweans seem to have given up here. It is stroked towards covers where the fielder fumbles and a run is taken.
Slightly short on middle, Sarkar pulls it through mid-wicket for a run.
SIX! Sarkar is now watching the ball like a football. Another biggie to his name. Dances down the track and lifts it over the mid-wicket fence. He is now one run short of Kayes' score.
Slightly shorter outside off, Kayes tries to work it on the leg side but it goes off the inner half through mid-wicket for another single.
Once again it is worked through mid-wicket for a run.
On the pads, the batsman works it through square leg for a single.
Wellington Masakadza is back on.
Kayes is happy waiting for the bad balls to hit a boundary and working the good balls around for singles. On a length around middle, the batsman works it through mid-wicket and collects a run.
Length ball around off, the batsman pushes it to covers. He wanted a run but is rightly sent back by his partner.
Delightful stroke! Does not go all the way but deserved a boundary. Full and on off, Kayes lunges and then times it through covers for a couple.
Now dances down the track and hits it over covers for a run. 150 up.
Nothing off the Free Hit though. Ngarava keeps it away from Sarkar's strong zone. He bowls it wide outside off, SS swings but misses.

FOUR! Off a NO BALL! To add to that it is a BOUNDARY! Slightly short on middle, Sarkar picks the length early and he pulls it over the mid-wicket fielder and one bounce into the fence. Free Hit coming up.
Sarkar is going after the bowlers. He makes room again and hits it, not off the middle though and it hits the stumps at the other end.
Ngarava is back on.
From around the wicket, he lands it on a length around off, the batsman guides it to point.
Down the leg side, it is a wide.
Another bumper, this one is well-directed. Kayes ducks under it.
Pulls it nicely but too close to the fine leg fielder. A run.
Fuller in length around off, the batter times it towards wide mid off for a run.
On a length and outside off, Sarkar guides it through backward point for a run.

FOUR! Welcome back into the attack. This is the first four after Powerplay 1. There were only sixes hit before this. Sarkar makes room and also comes down the track. He strokes it through extra cover and the ball races away.
Donald Tiripano is back on.
The physio is also out and the magic spray is being sprayed. It always does its work, doesn't it? Kayes is all ready to continue.

OUCH! That must have surely hurt. Sarkar dances down the track and bludgeons it back towards the non-striker. Kayes does not react in time and gets hit on the left elbow. He still manages to complete the single. However, he is holding his hand at the other end.
Slower through the air outside off, left alone.
Punched through covers for a run.
Hit hard and a couple. Short and outside off, Kayes cuts it through cover-point.
Down the leg side, wided.
Loopy ball on the stumps, kept out.
A half-tracker on middle, SS tries to pull but it goes off the inner half towards deep mid-wicket for a single.
Outside off, played towards cover-point for a run. 9 runs from the over. 157 more needed in 180 balls with 9 wickets in hand.
Shuffles right across and works it through mid-wicket for a single.
Flatter on middle, kept out.
Top edge but safe! Goes for the sweep but gets a top edge. It lands safe in the fine leg region. A run taken.

SIX! That is HUGE! Brings up his fifty in style. His 7th in ODIs. A good comeback knock for him and that too under pressure. He steps down the track and tonks it in the cow corner region. The timing is such that the ball goes all the way.
Floats it up on off, the batsman keeps it out.
Quicker and outside off, Kayes cuts it hard but finds the man at point.
Flatter outside off, Sarkar guides it towards short third man for a run.
Almost! Tosses it up on middle, Sarkar tries to defend but the ball hits the bottom part and rolls towards the keeper.
Down the leg side, another extra.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman. One run added to the total.
Down the leg side, the batsman misses the flick and it has been wided.
Another loopy ball on off, Kayes drives it to covers.
On the stumps, the batsman blocks it out.
Quicker again on middle, the batsman finds mid-wicket with his flick.
Fires it outside off, Kayes works it against the angle towards mid-wicket. Need to vary the pace a little, toss it up as it is too easy for the batters.
Tosses it up on middle, SS eases it down to long on for a run. He moves onto 45.
On the pads, Sarkar tries to sweep but gets it off the inner half towards short fine leg.
A yorker on middle, jammed out.
Fires it outside off, Kayes hits it through covers for a run.

WIDE! Harsh decision there as it seemed to have come off the bat. This was on the pads, it seemed as if, Kayes flicks it fine down the leg side. The batsmen take two. The umpire however feels it touched nothing and signals it as a wide.
Sean Williams is into the attack. Trying everything here is Masakadza.
Tosses it up outside off, Sarkar drives it to covers.
Fired on off, Sarkar keeps it out.

Misfield and a run! Every run is important for Zimbabwe at the moment, can't commit such mistakes. It is a shorter delivery outside off, Kayes guides it towards point. Tiripano there misfields and the batsmen take a run.
Fires it on middle, the batsman keeps it out.
Slightly shorter this time, Kayes off the back foot hits it through the off side. At the very end he opened the face and guides it past point and the batsmen take two.
Very full outside off, the ball is driven through covers for a run.

Drinks! Bangladesh are absolutely cruising at the moment. They did lose Das early but after that, the two batting out there have milked the bowlers. Zimbabwe need not one but a few wickets or the hosts will make a canter of this chase. Is there a fightback in store after the break or will the home side continue its domination?
A single to end a good over for Bangladesh. 10 from it as the ball is eased down to long on and Sarkar will retain strike.
Kayes now does the same thing and gets to the other end.
Sarkar is content in taking singles. He pushes it to long off for a run.
Now follows the biggie up with a run as he works it onto the leg side.

SIX! That should release all the pressure, if there was any building. Kayes brings out the slog sweep and he has nailed it right off the middle. It flies over the square leg fence for a biggie. 100 up and the two are moving along with ease. Zimbabwe need a wicket quickly or this pair will take the game away.
Fires it on the pads, it is worked with the angle through mid-wicket for no runs.

The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery. A good tight over by Raza. They need to bowl a few more like this and create pressure. That will hopefully buy them a wicket.
Gives it air on off, the batter strokes it down to long off for a run.
On the stumps again, defended.
Fires it on the stumps, Kayes keeps it out.
BEATEN! This is bowled quicker and slightly shorter outside off, Kayes goes back and tries to cut but misses. The keeper though fails to collect it.
Tosses it up on off, kept out.
On the pads again, Sarkar finds short fine leg with his flick. Two dots to end.
Fires it on middle, Sarkar with soft hands works it to mid-wicket.
On the pads it is easily clipped through square leg for a single.
Driven through mid on by the batsman. One run added to the total.
Fifty for Kayes. His 17th in this format. His purple patch in this series continues. Another important knock by the southpaw. He works this with the turn towards square leg for a single.
On the pads, the batsman works it through square leg for a run.
Gives this air around off, Sarkar hits it down to long off for a single.
Short and wide outside off, it skids off the surface. Kayes goes back and slaps it through covers. Only a run.
Shortish delivery on off, skidding back in, Sarkar cracks it off his back foot to sweeper cover for one.
Tossed up ball on off, driven down to long off for a run. Doing it with ease, these two.
Flighted and full on off, Kayes is on the front foot as he defends it to the leg side.
Raza drags his length short and bowl it outside off, Sarkar rocks back and whacks it to deep point for one.
Flighted and very full on middle, it's pushed down the ground to long on for a run.
Strides forward to a full ball and knocks it down through mid on for a run.
Played to mid-wicket by the batsman. No run.
A low full toss on off, it's driven through the line but straight to the cover fielder.
Another short delivery on middle, the batsman pulls it to deep backward square leg for a run.
Kayes goes back and works it with the turn through square leg for a run.
Double change as Wellington Masakadza is into the attack.
Spinning away from the batsman, on the shorter side, Kayes chases it and slaps it to deep cover for another run.
This time Sarkar forces it off his back foot to sweeper cover for a run.
Short and wide outside off, Sarkar goes for the cut shot but fails to middle it properly.
Flatter and on middle, worked on the leg side but straight to mid-wicket.
Tosses this up around off, Kayes eases it down to long off for a single.
Flatter and around off, Kayes guides it to point.
Powerplay 2 has been signaled! Now a maximum of 4 fielders can be placed outside the ring till the 40th over. Also, Sikandar Raza is into the attack.
Angling into the batsman, Sarkar works it off his pads towards wide mid on. 80/1 in Powerplay 1. A great beginning here by Bangladesh after losing a wicket off the first ball.
Bowls a low full toss way wide outside off, Sarkar reaches out for it and squeezes it to covers. It would have been called a wide had he left it alone.
Good length ball on middle and leg, it's turned through square leg for a run.
Wide called for height! A slower bouncer, Kayes ducks under it and Taylor experiences a bad bounce. Fails to collect it cleanly and gets hit on the knee. The ball deflects to his left and they cross.
Back of a length delivery on off, Sarkar tries to tap and run by pushing it towards cover-point. But he has hit it too well and hence no run taken.
Shortish and around off, Sarkar jumps out of the crease and drags his pull shot past the diving mid-wicket fielder. A couple of runs taken.
FOUR! Uppish but over the infield. Fullish and around off, Sarkar takes his front leg forward and lifts it over extra cover for a boundary. They are unstoppable at the moment.
Too straight in line, it's flicked through mid-wicket for an easy single. 10 coming from this over. 216 needed off 246 balls.
On a length and around off, Sarkar plays it down from the crease to covers.
Good length delivery outside off, Kayes slices his attempted cut shot past the point fielder. A run added to the total.

FOUR! Another boundary square of the wicket, this time on the off side. This is now the 12th boundary of the Bangladeshi innings. Short and wide outside off, Kayes shows no mercy and thwacks it through backward point for a boundary.
FOUR! Eased away! Jarvis bowls a length delivery outside the line of the leg stump. Kayes picks it off his pads and eases it past the right side of the short fine leg fielder for a boundary.
Good length delivery on middle and off, Kayes stays on the back foot and pushes it with an angled bat to cover-point.
Width on offer outside off, Kayes steers it through point and rotates the strike.
A little bit of movement back into the batsman from around off, Sarkar nudges it off the inner half of the bat to square leg for a run.
Turns a length ball on the leg side, finds the gap at mid-wicket and steals a single.
Outside off on a length, Sarkar dabs it down to point and picks up a brisk run.

FOUR! Whacked! Back of a length delivery outside off, plenty of width on offer there, Sarkar stands back and clobbers it through covers for a boundary. Runs coming thick and fast and Zimbabwe are looking completely clueless at the moment.
Played to the point region by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Donald Tiripano is into the attack now.
Pitches it up and around off, Imrul drives it to wide mid off and scampers across to the other end. The fielder has a shy at the bowler's end but misses. 14 from this over also.

EDGY FOUR! Once again there is width on offer outside off, Kayes tries to force the issue through the off side but it takes a thick outside edge and screams away to the third man fence. Jarvis is disappointed. 50 up for Bangladesh!

Shout for an lbw. The umpire turns it down. A length delivery in line of the stumps, Kayes tries to work it on the leg side but misses and is hit on the back thigh. They appeal but it's pitched outside leg. Physio comes out as Imrul is feeling some discomfort.
Imrul Kayes once again has got off to a start and is looking dangerous.

FOUR! Wow, this is exceptional hitting. The crowd is loving it. Kayes is just flourishing. He stays back to a shortish length delivery on off and plays a back foot punch in the air. It flies just over the cover-point fielder and reaches the fence in no time.
Played to the mid-wicket region by the batsman. One run added to the total.

FOUR! Three in a row now for Bangladesh. A bit lucky this time though. Jarvis dishes out a good length delivery outside off, Sarkar flashes his bat at it and the bottom edge scoots past the keeper to the third man fence.

FOUR! Bang! Imrul Kayes continuing with his rich vein of form. He gets the width again outside off to free his arms and crunches it through cover-point for a glorious boundary. 14 from the over, momentum has now shifted...
FOUR! Blasted away! No stopping this one. Ngarava feeds room outside off, the length is on the shorter side and Imrul hammers it over extra cover for a powerful boundary.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Shortish length ball outside off, Kayes stands tall and slaps it through extra cover. Chigumbura from mid off chases it down and saves two runs for his side.
Eyes the yorker but delivers it too full around off. Sarkar does well to clip it through mid-wicket for a single.
Wide! Once again Ngarava loses his line and slips one down the leg side. Too far away from the batsman to make any connection. A good take by Taylor.
Puts it on a full length around off, Kayes pushes inside the line and guides it past the point fielder for a run.
Imrul Kayes is taking the leg stump guard now.
Wide! Back of a length delivery sliding down the leg side, Sarkar tries flicking but misses.
Angling away from the batsman, it's outside off, an easy leave for the batsman this time.
A touch short in length again, around off, Sarkar punches it from the back foot but finds the point fielder.
A little short in length around off, Kayes moves back and turns it through the gap at mid-wicket for a run.
Flashes and misses! Jarvis tempts the batsman with a delivery outside off, the length is on the shorter side which prompts the batsman to go after it. Imrul throws his bat at it but fails to connect.
Serves it on a length around off. It stops a bit onto the batsman who bunts it towards mid off for a quick single.
Angling away from the batsman, outside off, Sarkar drives off the front foot but finds the cover fielder.
Back of a length ball on off, Sarkar stands tall and pulls it off the inner half of the bat through mid-wicket. A single taken. 16 from the last two overs, Bangladesh are now pressing on the gas.

FOUR! Once again aerial but right through the gap. A good length delivery in the channel outside off, Sarkar nicely gets on the front foot and cracks his drive through the gap between mid off and extra cover.
Full and angling into the batsman, from middle and leg, Sarkar tries flicking but misses.
Angling away from the batsman outside off, Kayes runs it down past the backward point fielder for a run.
Fetches a short ball from outside off but pulls it on the bounce to mid on.
Gets across the stumps and works it off the inner half of the bat to fine leg for a run.

Appeal for an lbw, not given. A delivery around middle and leg, Kayes fails to work it around the leg side and is hit on the pads. A big appeal follows but nothing from the umpire. Inside edge, the replays show later on.
FOUR! Shot! Once again it's aerial but over the infield. Jarvis angles across a short of a length delivery outside off. Kayes keeps himself on the back foot and lofts it over covers for a boundary.

In the air... safe! Jarvis offers width outside off and Sarkar throws his bat at it away from his body. His feet go nowhere and he ends up slicing it towards third man. Tiripano decides to wait for the ball to come at him rather than charging forward. A single take. Should have attempted to take the catch at least.
Lands it on a length and around off, angling away, Sarkar taps it down on the off side and looks for a run. This time Kayes is not interested.
Shortish and on off, punched from the back foot but straight to cover-point.
FOUR! Pulled away! Jarvis digs in a short delivery on middle, not much bounce, Sarkar gets on top of it and pummels it over mid-wicket. No one in the deep and it's a boundary.
A little short in length just outside off, Imrul taps it down towards cover-point and sets off for a run. But it's not on and his partner sends him back.
On a length around off, Imrul defends it back from the crease.
Brings this one back into the batsman from around off, Kayes covers the line and blocks.
FOUR! Risky but effective! Short and wide outside off, Kayes whacks it through the line and doesn't bother to keep it down. The point fielder flies to his left but it sneaks past him for a boundary.
The batsman has played it to the point region. One run added to the total.
Play and a miss! A gentle delivery, a bit short and outside off, Sarkar tries to cut it off his back foot but misses as the ball skids past the inside edge.
Richard Ngarava to bowl with the second new ball.

Cracked away but a great stop. Once again Jarvis delivers a shortish ball on off, Kayes blazes it away on the off side but the cover-point fielder dives across to his right to make an outstanding stop. Saves a certain boundary.
Shortish and on off, Kayes tries the back foot punch but fails to middle it properly. It goes rolling towards covers.
Skiddy delivery. It lands on a length in line of the stumps, Kayes is beaten for pace and is hit high on the back leg.
Shortish delivery, outside off, Sarkar flat-bats it through the line and the ball speeds through backward point. The third man fielder runs across to his left to stop the ball and they collect a run.
Back of a length delivery on off, Sarkar punches it off his back foot but finds the cover fielder.
Soumya Sarkar is the number 3 batsman.

OUT! It's clipping leg. The umpire's call stays and Bangladesh suffer and early blow. Jarvis serves a full length ball around off and gets it to move back into the batsman. Das tries to flick it across the line but misses to get hit on the pads. They appeal and the umpire raises his finger after thinking for a while. Liton Das walks up to his partner and then takes the DRS. The replays roll in and they find the impact to be in line and it's going on to brush the leg pole. Zimbabwe are delighted. A perfect beginning for them.
Huge shout for an lbw. The finger goes up. What a start for Zimbabwe! Liton Das, however, has referred it.

We're back for the run chase. The men concerned are back on the field. Imrul Kayes and Liton Das are the Bangladesh openers. Both have shown good form and are fresh from a 148-run stand. They would like to lay a strong platform in this stiff chase. Kyle Jarvis to begin proceedings with the first new ball. Let's play...
